items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: Dick Bock started the Pacific Jazz Record Company to record that group and immediately started to record them

ctx.x: Was there a financial incentive to keep the group together? Sometimes we make assumptions that these groups that find a niche and create a sound that they’re being rewarded monetarily?

I think that was — if it hadn’t already happened it was certainly coming, and it had happened to a degree because the crowds at The Haig, where they were playing, even though The Haig wasn’t very small — I mean there were literally people lined up around the block to get in. Dick Bock started the Pacific Jazz Record Company to record that group and immediately started to record them, and those records he couldn’t keep up with the demand for the records, and then immediately went up to San Francisco and played The…
